Each service (ProjectService, TaskService, UserService) depends on those ports through constructor injection and never calls Date or a UUID library directly, so no service bypasses the module's own abstractions. Entity construction and state changes stay in the domain (createProject, createUser, new Task, task.assignTo, task.markDone), so the services do not duplicate domain invariants. One small overlap exists: TaskService.requireProject repeats the project-existence check and the NotFoundError("Project", id) throw from ProjectService.get. This is a trivial repository-lookup guard, not a business rule or invariant, so it does not amount to a real split or duplication. TaskService.requireUser throws ValidationError for a missing assignee, while UserService.get throws NotFoundError. These are different meanings (an invalid assignee is not the same as a missing resource), so they are not a duplicated rule. The structure is consistent across all three services, and the module is cohesive.
